source.title: Fictional evaluation scenario
source.text: Fictional scenario, not a real study. A four-week email-reminder pilot with 40 volunteers observed attendance increase from 70% to 78%. There was no comparison group. Grades, communication skills, accessibility, enforcement costs and transport barriers were not measured. A separate survey of 100 students found 60 opposed mandatory attendance, 25 supported it and 15 were undecided. Students with documented illness could request exemptions.

claims.text: Recorded attendance rose by eight percentage points.
The pilot used a comparison group.
Email reminders caused attendance to increase.
Mandatory attendance had no effect on grades.
Most surveyed students opposed compulsory attendance.
Students with documented illness could not request exemptions.
Colleges should require attendance because it improves grades.
